downloadFlow.title: Step 1 of 3 — Scanning Link Safety...
downloadFlow.what: Ad interstitial. Faux 'SECURITY SCAN 1/3'. Button javascript:void(0) disabled by client JS for 5 seconds ('var timeLeft = 5;'), then becomes 'Continue to Link Generation →'. data-href = same URL + '&ad_done=1'.

downloadFlow.title: Step 2 of 3 — Generating Secure Link...
downloadFlow.what: Second 5s timer. The server-rendered HTML already contains the plaintext final destination in data-href, i.e. decryption is server-side. No client-side decoder, no atob.

conditionalRequests.why: 304 costs no origin render and no body; unchanged catalog becomes tiny 304s instead of full renders

caching.rule: never re-fetch a page whose modified <= fetched_at

identifiers.secondary: slug (treat slug change on same id as rename, not new title)

errorHandling.on_exhaust: abort the whole run, persist state, alert human, 24h cooldown

userAgent.tradeoff: honest UA may be scored lower and challenged sooner; correct response is to stop, not spoof

triggers: cf page shape: server cloudflare + text/html + no wp-content in body
killSwitch.action: stop immediately, log URL, exit without retry, 24h cooldown

doNotDo: No parallel hammering (concurrency > 1, xargs -P, worker pools, retry storms)
No scraping of download/shortener/stream endpoints (codedew, hubcloud, gamerxyt, mega, argon)
No bypassing paywalls, ad gates, 5s timers, or Cloudflare challenges
No downloading, mirroring, rehosting or proxying the .mkv files
No bulk use of wp-json (noindex + no-store) and no touching /wp-admin/
No UA spoofing or cookie replay to look human
No copying their prose, episode descriptions or hosted posters into the app
No account creation, comments or contact-form submissions
No rendering the ad-gated download chain in an in-app WebView

verdict.summary: Ingest catalog metadata (title, season, episode/absolute number, language tags, declared quality set, TMDB poster id, post id/slug for attribution) and resolve nothing at scrape time; deep-link playback to the source in a Custom Tab. Do not mirror files and do not automate the download chain. This keeps nightly cost at ~18 edge-cached requests (~247 weekly), stays inside robots.txt, and leaves the distribution act with the operator.

pros: resilient to TLD rotation and token expiry
cons: worse UX (extra taps, visible ads, no offline downloads)
quality is a declared set, not per-file
does not by itself make the app lawful — catalogue still routes users to unlicensed dubs

verdict.hard_line: Mirroring the 208 MB .mkv files is technically trivial and legally the line between a metadata complaint and a criminal copyright case. Do not.
